thread:
DeployBot: :rotating_light: canary healthcheck failed in eu-west-1 for release/2026-03-15T14:00Z. 6/6 canary requests returned 502/503. Auto-rollback triggered and traffic routed to stable.
Jen (oncall): I'm on it. Paging infra and SRE. @Raj @Olivia can you join? Any idea what change was in this canary?
Raj: That canary included the KMS rotation handling and renamed env var (NEW_KMS_KEY_ID -> NEW_KMS_KEY) in the service. I thought the values file was updated, but the canary override used the old key name. Looking now.
Olivia: can we get logs from the failing pods? tagging @Jamie to surface any customer tickets.
DeployBot: canary: service=api-gateway pod=api-canary-7 logs: "error=KMSAccessDenied msg=AccessDeniedException: User arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-canary-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/"
Jen (oncall): that looks like an empty key id in the ARN. Raj, did the template change the env var name?
Raj: yep. Code reads NEW_KMS_KEY_ID but the helm canary values used NEW_KMS_KEY. So runtime had no KEY_ID -> client constructed arn with trailing slash -> KMS returns AccessDenied. I'm rolling back the canary values now.
Olivia: two quick mitigations: 1) flip the routing flag to stop sending traffic to the canary; 2) revert the canary chart values and run a validated canary after fixing env var names. Also check whether the canary role actually has kms:Decrypt permission for the intended key.
Jen (oncall): flipping kill-switch for routing.new_kms_flow now. Oncall action: run downgrade script and confirm traffic to stable.
Raj: toggled the feature flag via internal API: ```sh
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"routing.new_kms_flow","value":false}' https://flags.internal/toggle
``` 
Olivia: admin UI confirms canary at 0% traffic, stable 100%. Error rates dropping.
Jamie (support): support note: spike observed from 14:03 to 14:10 UTC, ~40 distinct API keys, mostly resolved after rollback. I'm preparing customer notifications for top impacted accounts.
Jen (oncall): setting incident severity sev2 (partial impact, mitigated). Timeline and actions to log in the incident doc. Next steps: - revert canary values (PR coming) - add CI lint to catch env var mismatches - add pre-deploy check that validates required env vars exist in the canary manifest - no key-policy change expected unless further evidence
Raj: opening PR #5460 to revert canary values and adding a unit test to flag missing NEW_KMS_KEY_ID in chart values. I'll run a dry KMS check before re-canary: ```sh
aws kms describe-key --key-id "$NEW_KMS_KEY_ID" --region eu-west-1
``` expecting 200.
Olivia: grabbed a live canary pod env to confirm: ```
kubectl exec -n prod api-canary-7 -- printenv | grep NEW_KMS
# no output
``` App logs show it built arn: `arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/` which KMS rejected.
Jen (oncall): IAM/role review: canary role does include kms:Decrypt on the intended key, but because the arn had no key id the request failed. So no policy change needed.
IncidentBot: Reminder: if you handoff, please update next oncall. Current oncall: Jen until 14:30 UTC.
Raj: I'll monitor for 30m, then merge the revert and re-run a validated canary with corrected variables and a dry-run KMS describe-key. If that passes we'll proceed.
Jamie (support): notified top-5 affected customers, posted to support and billing channels. No urgent escalations so far.
Jen (oncall): handing off to Raj at 14:28 UTC. Summary: canary failed due to env var name mismatch causing empty KMS key id -> malformed ARN -> AccessDenied. Mitigation: feature flag kill-switch flipped, traffic back to stable. Action items: revert canary values (PR #5460), add deploy pipeline checks, update canary runbook. Estimated customer impact window: 14:03-14:12 UTC (~9 minutes), ~40 API keys affected.
Raj: acknowledged, will post stability update in 15m and drive the follow-ups.
Olivia: filing follow-ups: INFRA-1982 (deploy sanity checker), DEVEX-403 (helm lint rule for env var names), SRE-77 (canary runbook updates). Assigning owners.
Jen (oncall): closing the incident thread for now, keeping pinned. Reopen if error rates rise.
IncidentBot: Incident marked RESOLVED by automated checks. :white_check_mark:
Jen (oncall): thanks all. Postmortem owners: Raj (author), Olivia (SRE reviewer), Jamie (customer comms).
